title: ChatGPT and large language models in academia: opportunities and challenges
extended_summary:
This editorial examines the emergence of ChatGPT and other large language models (LLMs) and argues that they represent a major shift in how text can be generated, edited, and used in academic work. The paper focuses on opportunities and risks rather than reporting an empirical study. It discusses how LLMs may support academic writing, education, programming, grant writing, and peer review, while also raising concerns about hallucinations, plagiarism, bias, access, and environmental cost.

In education, the authors emphasize possible uses of ChatGPT as a classroom aid, interactive study guide, writing assistant, and feedback tool. They suggest it may be especially helpful for non-native English speakers as a writing and editing support, and they also describe how educators might adapt assignments and assessments in response to student use of LLMs. The paper is framed around students and educators across K-12 and higher education, but it does not present data from a specific school, grade level, or instructional setting.

The authors conclude that LLMs should be embraced as useful tools, but only with careful attention to bias, accuracy, disclosure, and ethical use. They argue that LLM outputs should be checked, that bias metrics are needed, and that LLM-generated text should not automatically be treated as plagiarism. Overall, the paper is a position piece that outlines likely educational applications and cautions, rather than testing effects on learning outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot for generating and revising text, answering questions, and supporting interactive dialogue.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a general-purpose generative AI chatbot for academic writing, education, programming, and as an example of LLM use in K-12 and higher education contexts; no empirical evaluation of K-12 literacy outcomes in this paper.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an editorial/opinion piece rather than an empirical study. It discusses ChatGPT's potential uses and risks, but does not report original data, a study design, or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No impact effect can be estimated because the paper provides no outcome data or effect sizes. The discussion is conceptual only.
